transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herfst.
President Trump says he's rejecting a short-term Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
after seven days.
The proposed plan would also have temporarily ended hostilities in order to restart ceasefire
talks with the United States.
And here's Emily Fang has more.
Iran had proposed the plan this week at the United Nations General Assembly meetings in
New York, a plan very similar to a memorandum of understanding that the two countries agreed
upon back in June.
And Iran's president told CBS News he'd allow UN nuclear inspectors into Iran if there
were a long-term ceasefire deal with the U.S.
But Trump wrote on True Social Saturday morning, "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon," and
then told reporters before departing for Tennessee that the plan was "not acceptable."
Trump claimed Iran was negotiating out of a position of weakness and said they were "dying."
Emily Fang in Pierre News, Washington.
Former Kennedy Center employees say several months ago the institution's leadership canceled
a plan to repair significant leaks in the main building.
The center's board now says those leaks were so urgent that the complex had to close immediately.
And Pierre's Anastasia Sialakis has more.
In a letter sent to two congressional committees, the whistleblowers say the center's current
executive director, Matt Flocca, had secured $9.3 million to replace and repair water leaks
in the center's roof and soffits.
Those repairs were approved in August 2025, according to supplemental documents also filed
with Congress.
But this April, the whistleblowers say Flocca canceled the repair plan four months before
the Kennedy Center's board approved shutting the arts complex immediately.
They also say some of the waterproofing funds were diverted for repainting exterior columns
and other cosmetic changes President Trump desired.
The Kennedy Center did not respond immediately to NPR's request for comment.
Anastasia Sialakis, NPR News.
Hurricanes are churning in the Pacific today.
Hurricane NOLO is nearly stationary south of the Big Island of Hawaii and is expected
to strengthen over the next couple of days as it stays well south of Hawaii.
Adrian Montalvo says he's preparing for the hurricane by filling sandbags.
For an area that floods, we want to try to protect it.
Frank Ferreira is a meteorologist with the National Weather Service.
There is the potential for significant rainfall and possible flooding, especially for portions
of the Big Island, where they could see several inches up to a foot of rain in some spots.
Hurricane watches and tropical storm watches and warnings are up for parts of the Hawaiian
Islands.
Hurricane POLO is an extremely dangerous storm off the coast of Mexico and is expected to
make landfall on Monday.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Cleveland Orchestra has gone on strike.
As NPR's Eva Pukach reports, concerts have been canceled and the orchestra's European
tour is in doubt.
The Cleveland Orchestra is one of the big five American symphony orchestras.
Its musicians went on strike Friday.
The Cleveland Orchestra says the musicians' union asked for a 25% increase in salaries
over the next three years, which the orchestra says it could not meet.
The Cleveland Orchestra was preparing for a nine-country European tour beginning in
Germany next week.
A decision on whether the tour will proceed will be made by Sunday evening, Eva Pukach
and PR News.
The White House told Congress last night it plans to cancel more than $800 million in
money that lawmakers already approved for education and health-related programs.
It's the Trump administration's latest attempt to use a legally untested power to rescind
spending without lawmaker approval.
The rescission appears to target education for migrants, along with health research at
the Department of Health and Human Resources.
Lawmakers in both parties criticized the action, including Republican Senator Susan Collins,
who says the action usurps congressional appropriation powers.
Russian attacks on Ukraine today left at least eight people dead as Moscow hammered Ukraine
with crews and ballistic missiles, drones and guide bombs.
That's some four and a half years after Russia started the war that shows no signs of ending.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump rejects Iran's short-term plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz after seven days
Kennedy Center leadership canceled urgent roof leak repairs months before emergency closure, whistleblowers say
Hurricane NOLO strengthens south of Hawaii's Big Island, bringing potential for significant rainfall
Hurricane POLO strengthens off Mexico coast, expected to make landfall Monday
Cleveland Orchestra musicians strike over salary dispute, European tour in doubt
White House plans to cancel over $800 million in congressionally approved education and health funding
Russian attacks on Ukraine kill at least eight people with missiles, drones and guided bombs
